subtitle: Stories of a floating world and a deer that walks on water

panels.shot: wide aerial dusk shot over a mosaic of floating phumdi, with a lone deer and a fisher in frame
panels.action: Loktak Fisher of Moirang stands in a dugout canoe, pole poised, amid vast circular phumdi and a distant Sangai silhouette on the floating grassland, as mist curls over the lake and blue hills ring the horizon.

dialogue.text: On Loktak, houses float, deer walk on water, and a whole people balance between hunger and flood. This is the living story of the lake that breathes.

i18n.hi: लोकtak पर घर तैरते हैं, हिरन पानी पर चलते हैं, और एक पूरा समाज भूख और बाढ़ के बीच डोलता है। ये है साँस लेती झील की ज़िंदा कहानी।

panels.shot: slow push-in from above onto the lake surface transforming with seasons
panels.action: A sequence-like view shows Loktak Lake in three bands: swollen with monsoon, shrinking in dry months, and studded with thickening phumdi mats, while Loktak Fisher of Moirang rows through changing water levels.

dialogue.text: Year after year, Loktak grows and shrinks with the sky. The water climbs into fields, then retreats, leaving thick mats of roots and reeds drifting like islands.

i18n.hi: हर साल लोकtak आसमान के साथ बढ़ती–घटती है। पानी खेतों तक चढ़ आता है, फिर लौट जाता है, जड़–सरकंडों की मोटी चटाइयाँ छोड़कर जो टापुओं-सी बहती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot at water level, focused on hands lifting phumdi
panels.action: Kneeling in a canoe, Loktak Fisher of Moirang grips a chunk of phumdi, its tangled roots dripping, as another fisher steadies the boat among reeds and open water.

dialogue.text: The people of Moirang learned to read this breathing lake. They cut and shaped the drifting phumdi, turning wild plant mats into tools, fields and shelter.

i18n.hi: मोइरांग के लोगों ने इस साँस लेती झील को पढ़ना सीख लिया। वो बहते फुमदी काटते–गढ़ते, जंगली पौधों की चादर को औज़ार, खेत और ठिकानों में बदल देते।

panels.shot: wide tranquil dawn shot showing phumshang settlement
panels.action: Under a pale dawn, several phumshang huts stand on thick phumdi platforms tied together, smoke rising from a cooking fire as Loktak Fisher of Moirang steps from canoe onto the gently rocking surface.

dialogue.text: On these living rafts they raised phumshang huts. Floors of woven bamboo, walls of thatch, all resting on floating earth that sways when a child runs or a storm kicks the waves.

i18n.hi: इन ज़िंदा बेड़ों पर उन्होंने फुमशांग झोपड़ियाँ बसाईं। बांस की बुनी फ़र्श, घास की दीवारें, सब तैरती मिट्टी पर, जो बच्चे की दौड़ या तूफ़ान की लहर से ही डोल उठती है।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of circular athapum structures in the lake
panels.action: From above, circular and oval athapum fish enclosures made of arranged phumdi and reed fences form a pattern on the water, while Loktak Fisher of Moirang poles a canoe along the rim of one circle.

dialogue.text: They built athapum—floating rings that lure fish into a quiet trap. No stone embankments, no iron gates. Just reeds, roots and patience, drifting where the fish and currents move.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने अठपुम बनाये—तैरते घेरे जो मछलियों को चुपचाप जाल में खींच लाते। न पत्थर के बाँध, न लोहे के फाटक; बस सरकंडा, जड़ें और सब्र, वहीं बहते जहाँ मछली और धार जाए।

panels.shot: low wide shot of boat race from the shoreline perspective
panels.action: Along the shore near Moirang, long narrow boats slice through the lake in a race, rowers in unison, while Loktak Fisher of Moirang watches from a smaller canoe amid cheering villagers on the bank.

dialogue.text: Court chronicles like the Cheitharol Kumbaba remember Moirang for its boats and water games. For valley kings, these waters were pride and power; for fishers, they were bread and breath.

i18n.hi: चैथारोल कुम्बाबा जैसी दरबारी किताबें मोइरांग को उसकी नौकाओं और पानी के खेलों के लिए याद रखती हैं। घाटी के राजाओं के लिए ये पानी शान और ताक़त थे; मछुआरों के लिए वही रोटी और जान।

panels.shot: medium shot under overcast sky, fisher adjusting a net, hills in background
panels.action: Clouds gather over Loktak as Loktak Fisher of Moirang repairs a fishing net on a phumdi edge, the green hills of Manipur rising beyond and a faint temple-like structure on distant higher ground.

dialogue.text: No inscription dates the first phumshang. The record is the living routine: nets at dawn, offerings to the water, stories of storms that carried away homes and of returns to rebuild on the same drifting ground.

i18n.hi: पहले फुमशांग की तारीख कोई फ़रमान नहीं लिखता। असली दस्तावेज़ है रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी: सुबह जाल, पानी को अर्पण, आंधियों की कथाएँ जो घर बहा ले गईं, और लौटकर उसी बहती ज़मीन पर फिर से बसने की कहानियाँ।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Sangai on phumdi with fisher in the distant background
panels.action: A Sangai deer stands poised on a thick phumdi in Keibul Lamjao, its delicate hooves pressing the springy mat, while far behind, barely visible, Loktak Fisher of Moirang paddles along the edge of the floating grassland.

dialogue.text: On the southern fringe lies Keibul Lamjao, the world’s only floating national park. Here the Sangai, Manipur’s brow-antlered deer, steps softly on phumdi that shifts under each careful hoof.

i18n.hi: दक्षिणी किनारे पर है केइबुल लामजाओ, दुनिया का इकलौता तैरता राष्ट्रीय उद्यान। यहीं संगाई, मणिपुर का भूरा सींग वाला हिरन, फुमदी पर हल्के क़दम रखता है जो हर संभली चाल के नीचे हिलती रहती है।

panels.shot: tight shot of fisher’s face watching a distant Sangai at sunset
panels.action: At sunset, Loktak Fisher of Moirang sits still in his canoe, eyes fixed on a distant Sangai against the orange sky, as birds circle above the reed beds and the water glows.

dialogue.speaker: the_fisherfolk_of_loktak
dialogue.text: If the phumdi sinks, both our lives go under.

i18n.hi: अगर फुमदी डूबी, तो हमारी भी साँस रुक जाएगी।

panels.shot: archival-style montage shot with split frame: old and new
panels.action: In a split scene, one side shows Loktak Fisher of Moirang in traditional dress casting a net, the other side shows a modern concrete barrage gate and power lines over the same lake waters.

dialogue.text: Then came concrete and control. Ithai barrage held the waters high for power and irrigation, but the lake that once rose and fell with the seasons was pinned to a new rhythm.

i18n.hi: फिर आया कंक्रीट और क़ाबू। ईथाइ बाँध ने बिजली और सिंचाई के लिए पानी ऊँचा बाँध दिया, और जो झील पहले मौसमों के साथ उठती–गिरती थी, उसे नई रिवायत से बाँध दिया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot from bank showing raised waterline against trees and homesteads
panels.action: Water laps high against tree trunks and a partly submerged old path, as Loktak Fisher of Moirang stands on a flooded veranda, looking out toward his phumshang now moored closer to the village edge.

dialogue.text: Reports note what the eye already saw. Higher water levels buried fields, changed fish routes, and kept phumdi afloat longer on the surface instead of resting on the lakebed in dry months.

i18n.hi: रिपोर्टों ने वही लिखा जो आँखें पहले देख चुकी थीं। ऊँचे पानी ने खेत डुबो दिए, मछलियों के रास्ते बदले, और फुमदी को सूखे में तलहटी पर टिकने की बजाय सतह पर ही ज़्यादा देर तैराए रखा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Keibul Lamjao showing thinning phumdi and concerned figures in distance
panels.action: Across Keibul Lamjao, patches of open water cut into the floating grassland, the phumdi visibly thinner, while Loktak Fisher of Moirang and a forest guard stand on a boat, surveying the fragile expanse.

dialogue.text: Scientists and lake dwellers watched the Sangai’s ground soften. With altered water regimes, phumdi in the park thinned and shifted, its weight and thickness no longer following the old cycle of sinking and rising.

i18n.hi: वैज्ञानिक और झील के लोग संगाई की ज़मीन को नरम होते देखते रहे। बदले हुए पानी के दौर ने उद्यान की फुमदी को पतला और डगमग बना दिया, उसका वज़न और मोटाई अब पुराने डूबने–उभरने के चक्र से नहीं चलती थी।

panels.shot: documentary-style medium shot of fisher at a meeting with officials, maps behind
panels.action: Inside a modest hall, Loktak Fisher of Moirang sits among other fishers facing officials with maps of the lake on the wall, lines marking phumdi zones, power projects and protected areas.

dialogue.text: The lake became a meeting table. Fishers spoke of rights and eviction, officials of weed control and power, conservationists of Sangai numbers and water quality. The same water lay behind every argument.

i18n.hi: झील एक बैठक की मेज़ बन गई। मछुआरे हक़ और बेदखली की बात करते, अफ़सर खरपतवार और बिजली की, संरक्षणकर्ता संगाई की गिनती और पानी की सफ़ाई की। हर बहस के पीछे यही एक पानी था।

panels.shot: insert shot of official documents and a globe, with Loktak in focus
panels.action: A close view of hands turning pages of a Ramsar Convention document and a Loktak Development Authority report, with a small globe in the background and a pin marking Manipur.

dialogue.text: In 1990, the Ramsar Convention listed Loktak as a wetland of international importance. In 1993, it entered the Montreux Record, named among sites where change had placed the ecosystem under strain.

i18n.hi: 1990 में रामसर कन्वेंशन ने लोकtak को अंतरराष्ट्रीय अहमियत वाली आर्द्रभूमि माना। 1993 में वो मॉन्त्रॉ रजिस्टर में गया, उन जगहों में जिनके बदलते रूप ने वहाँ के तंत्र को दबाव में डाल दिया था।

panels.shot: wide shot of lake showing both pollution and traditional activity
panels.action: On one side of the frame, plastic and hyacinth choke a cove near concrete houses; on the other, Loktak Fisher of Moirang tends an athapum, while distant smoke plumes rise from lakeside settlements.

dialogue.text: Pollution flowed from towns, pesticides from fields, silt from hills. Yet among this, phumdi still held up huts and nets, and the lake people still turned floating weed into food and income.

i18n.hi: शहरों से गंदगी, खेतों से कीटनाशक, पहाड़ियों से मिट्टी बहकर आई। फिर भी फुमदी अब भी झोपड़ियाँ और जाल थामे रही, और झील के लोग अब भी तैरती घास को खाने और रोज़ी में बदलते रहे।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot inside a phumshang at night
panels.action: Inside a gently rocking phumshang, a lantern lights Loktak Fisher of Moirang sitting with family, the bamboo floor flexing slightly, shadows of water ripples dancing on the walls.

dialogue.speaker: the_fisherfolk_of_loktak
dialogue.text: The reports write our lake, but they do not feel this sway.

i18n.hi: रिपोर्टें हमारी झील लिखती हैं, पर ये डोलना महसूस नहीं करतीं।

panels.shot: sunrise wide shot of fisher and Sangai sharing the landscape
panels.action: At sunrise, Loktak Fisher of Moirang poles his canoe past the edge of Keibul Lamjao, while a Sangai browses on nearby phumdi, both figures mirrored in the still, golden water.

dialogue.text: The fisher and the deer remain tied to the same floating earth, each step testing the strength of the mat beneath, each season waiting to see how the lake will choose to breathe next.

i18n.hi: मछुआरा और हिरन दोनों एक ही तैरती ज़मीन से बँधे हैं, हर क़दम में नीचे की चटाई की मज़बूती परखते, हर मौसम में देखते हैं कि अगली बार झील कैसी साँस लेगी।

panels.shot: lingering high-angle shot over Loktak showing mosaic of human and wild spaces
panels.action: From high above, Loktak spreads out like a living map—phumshang clusters, athapum circles, open channels, and the dense green of Keibul Lamjao—while Loktak Fisher of Moirang’s canoe is a tiny line on the water.

dialogue.text: Loktak’s story asks a quiet question: can our grand engineering learn from this modest craft, where infrastructure floats, yields and adjusts, and survival depends on listening to a lake that still breathes?

i18n.hi: लोकtak की कहानी एक धीमा सवाल पूछती है: क्या हमारी बड़ी इंजीनियरिंग इस छोटे हुनर से सीख सकती है, जहाँ ढाँचे तैरते, झुकते और ढलते हैं, और ज़िंदगी एक ऐसी झील की सुनने पर टिकी है जो अब भी साँस लेती है?

subtitle_i18n.en: Stories of a floating world and a deer that walks on water
subtitle_i18n.hi: तैरती दुनिया की दास्तान, और वो हिरन जो पानी पर चलता है
